caseObservations.observations: Alex’s competing assignments make prioritisation, realistic breaks and support concrete. The plan comparison distinguishes immediate relief from postponed tasks; the worked answer gives a feasible two-block plan and a later review. Preventive effects are probabilistic. The fresh task removes deadline flexibility and delegation, requiring adjustment of resources rather than a number substitution. The 4/4/2 rubric allocates points to explained skills, plan/comparison and revised conditions. Learner reasoning must be produced before the worked answer is used; the supplied answer itself is not learner evidence.

Samira’s group-pressure situation changes the demand from organising work to balancing relationships and self-protection. The task asks for reasoned strategies and several sources of satisfaction. Calm boundaries, alternatives and leaving persistent pressure are defensible options; responsibility for pressure is assigned to those applying it. The online-team transfer changes social constraints and availability, without diagnosing media addiction. The rubric rewards action links, limits and transfer. DE/EN preserve the same constraints.

Comparable playing time in A and B prevents a duration threshold from solving the task. Failed stopping attempts, missed commitments and distress make B’s indicators distinct from A’s reported control and functioning. The solution explicitly stops short of diagnosis and allows an optional general risk question and help. A longer planned single event changes the persistence/context condition, so the transfer requires reasoning beyond a time cut-off. The 4/4/2 rubric matches comparison, voluntary risk reflection and single-event interpretation.

Music enjoyment versus substance use despite consequences gives a changed subject matter while retaining control/consequences reasoning. The two comment claims are appropriately challenged: enjoyment is insufficient and a weak-will label is not an explanation. The solution bounds help and excludes unsupervised withdrawal. A concern without personal disclosure is an information-limited transfer: general criteria and confidential help remain possible, while a diagnosis from silence is unjustified. This transfer establishes limits of inference, not actual clinical risk or private self-knowledge.

Together with both full cases these cover explanation and derivation without requiring proof of lifestyle change.

e1 distinguishes pleasure/frequency from control/impact criteria; e2 relates risk awareness to voluntary reflection/help; e3 requires transfer and recognition of information limits. Both full cases retain non-diagnostic interpretation and DE/EN equivalence.

sourceObservations.observedPrimaryLocation: B8 Lernbereich 5, first and third competence bullets in the actual HTML
sourceObservations.sourceAssessment: Direct complete competence anchor for the two canonical descriptions. The first bullet connects enjoyment/addiction explanation with risk awareness; the third connects life skills, coping, satisfaction and deriving personal-development strategies. The separate second bullet supplies the model-based addiction-development neighbour. SourceRef suffixes .1/.3 are local bullet locators, not officially numbered subtopics.

sourceObservations.observedPrimaryLocation: Physical/printed page 31, actual PDF with 2022 validity overlay
sourceObservations.sourceAssessment: The official operator for effects of alcohol/drugs and prevention strategies is nennen. The authored source operationalisation erklären/ableiten is stronger and must not be quoted as official wording. The source supplies a preventive-strategy subset; it does not spell out the full BY enjoyment-boundary or life-skills/personal-development contracts. The supplied mappings are partial and are retained as partial in this review.

sourceObservations.observedPrimaryLocation: Actual restriction annex, physical page 1 and following retained content
sourceObservations.sourceAssessment: The 2022 annex explicitly carries the existing Sinne und Wahrnehmung standards into end-of-year-9 requirements and includes the same nennen wording for alcohol/drugs and prevention. Thus the displayed SekI route has a real restriction document binding; the old end-of-year-10 heading alone must not be used as the effective current year claim.

sourceObservations.observedPrimaryLocation: Physical page 24, printed page 20, Nervensystem table
sourceObservations.sourceAssessment: Mandatory drugs and prevention plus an example of reflecting on health/social responsibility support a bounded risk/prevention subset. Notes include personal/social consequences and other addictive potentials such as persistent phone/computer use. They do not prescribe the full life-skills operator sequence or a clinical diagnostic test. Partial evidence is appropriate; the illustrative classroom cases must not be described as measurements or trials.

sourceObservations.observedPrimaryLocation: Physical pages 34–36, printed pages 22–24, actual tables visually inspected at 34 and 36
sourceObservations.sourceAssessment: The compulsory area asks for judging addiction dangers with substances, internet/social media and physical/psychological/social consequences. This supports criterion-based risk explanation; an exact counterpart of the BY third bullet is absent here. Stress and stress management is explicitly Wahlbereich 1 on physical page 36; that optional block cannot alone establish mandatory universal life-skills coverage. Source status remains partial without importing unrelated neighbouring hormone/sexuality clauses.

sourceObservations.observedPrimaryLocation: Physical/printed pages 38–39, actual competence table viewed at 38
sourceObservations.sourceAssessment: Discussing addiction behaviour and deriving healthy-living conclusions, evaluating addiction/stress risk factors, and evaluating group norms/stressors provide substantial risk/coping intersections. Page 39 adds stress-avoidance measures. These are broader combined standards rather than exact independent copies of either BY competency; the mappings remain partial.

sourceObservations.observedPrimaryLocation: Physical pages 22–24, printed pages 16–18, actual primary pages 22 and 24 viewed
sourceObservations.sourceAssessment: Physical 22 provides measures to maintain health, including avoiding misuse of substances. Physical 24 contains self/social competences such as accepting/giving help, dealing with setbacks/conflicts and reflecting on behaviour. This permits bounded supporting context for prevention/skill choices, while separate self/social clauses must not be re-labelled as an official addiction-specific personality-development contract. Partial mappings are maintained.

supplementaryFactualCheck.method: web search and direct open during this run
supplementaryFactualCheck.purpose: Check that educational warning indicators and non-diagnostic limits in gaming case are factually compatible.
supplementaryFactualCheck.observation: WHO identifies impaired control, priority over other activities and continuation despite negative consequences; diagnostic classification also requires significant impairment and usually prolonged persistence. The classroom material uses indicators rather than assigning diagnoses from time or enjoyment alone. This scientific cross-check supplies no curriculum jurisdiction mapping.
